question: Should Browser geolocation set requests with malformed or non-HTTP(S) explicit origins now fail immediately with HTTP 400 instead of retaining the prior partial-success or adapter-time behavior?
rationale: The implementation is correct, but this caller-visible error-timing change is an intentional compatibility choice that CI cannot decide.

options.title: Accept strict route validation
options.body: Adopt the early HTTP 400 because a request with an invalid explicit origin cannot correctly grant the requested site permission.

options.title: Preserve legacy partial behavior
options.body: Keep setting coordinates when origin is invalid and separately report or ignore permission-grant failure, retaining a less coherent contract.

recommendation.title: Accept strict route validation
recommendation.body: Adopt the early HTTP 400 because a request with an invalid explicit origin cannot correctly grant the requested site permission.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the current route behavior and owns the canonical takeover branch.
